data.sourceWord: MCQ: Which one of the following was the first prophet in Islam?

examples.en-GB: AQA MCQ (1 mark) — Answer: Adam | Distractors: Ismail; Musa; Nuh

data.targetWord: Muslims believe Ibrahim was sent by God to establish monotheism, is known as the friend of Allah, broke the idols, and rebuilt the Ka'aba with his son Ismail.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — beliefs about the Prophet Ibrahim

data.targetWord: Muslims believe Ibrahim was tested by God, willing to sacrifice his son in obedience, making him a supreme role model of faith and trust in Allah.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — beliefs about the Prophet Ibrahim

data.targetWord: Many Sunni Muslims believe Allah has decreed all that happens, recorded on the Tablet of Decrees; this gives comfort in hardship, trusting all comes from Allah.

examples.en-GB: 'Only what God has decreed will happen to us.' (9:51)

data.targetWord: Muslims also believe they have free will and are judged on their choices, so belief in predestination encourages them to perform good, creditworthy actions.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.3 (4 marks) — influence of predestination

data.targetWord: Justice (Adl) is one of Allah's 99 names and a Root of Shi'a faith; Muslims believe God will hold everyone to account on the Day of Judgement so fairness prevails.

examples.en-GB: 'Surely Allah wrongs not even of the weight of an atom.' (4:40)

data.targetWord: Because God is just, Muslims must mirror this by giving to charity, helping the poor and standing up for just causes, hoping for God's justice in the hereafter.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.4 (5 marks) — beliefs about God's justice

data.targetWord: 'O you who believe, be upright for God, and be bearers of witness with justice.' (5:8) — commanding Muslims to stand firmly for justice as a witness to God.

data.sourceWord: FOR: Qur'an is the direct word of Allah
data.targetWord: The Qur'an is the direct, unaltered word of Allah, protected by him: 'Verily we have revealed it and we are the protectors of it.' (15:9), making it uniquely authoritative.

data.sourceWord: FOR: Qur'an is a complete guide for life
data.targetWord: The Qur'an is a comprehensive code of life and the main source of Shari'ah; those who do not judge by it are warned in 5:44, so it stands above other sources.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Hadith is needed for practice
data.targetWord: The Qur'an does not detail how to perform Salah or Zakah; the Hadith is essential to show how rituals are carried out, suggesting it is equally vital.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Modern life needs more guidance
data.targetWord: Revealed over 1400 years ago, the Qur'an does not directly address modern issues like IVF or the internet; for Shi'a Muslims the Imam also holds great authority.

data.answer: Allah is just and brings everyone to justice.

data.title: Tawhid: The Oneness of God in Islam
data.sourceTitle: Tawhid: The Oneness of God in Islam
data.sourcePassage: Tawhid, the oneness of God, is the most important belief in Islam. Muslims believe in one God, Allah, who is the creator and sustainer of everything and has no partners or equals. This absolute monotheism shapes the whole of Muslim life. Because Allah alone is worshipped, Muslims reject any form of idolatry (shirk), which is considered the gravest sin. Allah is described through the 99 Names, which include the Just, the Merciful and the All-Knowing. Belief in Tawhid means Muslims trust that everything happens according to Allah's will, while still holding that humans have free will and will be judged for their actions on the Day of Judgement. The Qur'an, believed to be the direct word of Allah revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, is the central source of authority for understanding and living out Tawhid.
